subject: Logic
title: The Conjunction Fallacy
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Conjunction Fallacy.

hook.text: Linda is a bank teller. Linda is a feminist bank teller. Which is more probable? Most people pick wrong.

buildup.text: The conjunction fallacy: thinking A AND B is more likely than A alone. Mathematically impossible.

discovery.text: Kahneman and Tversky showed that adding details makes a story more believable but less probable.

twist.text: "Bank teller" includes all bank tellers—feminist ones and non-feminist ones. The subset can't be bigger.

climax.text: Our brains prefer detailed, coherent stories over raw probabilities. Narrative beats math every time.

quiz.question: Why is A AND B never more probable than A alone?
options: The conjunction is a subset of A
